title: Mental Health Support
goal: Ask for support, describe your experience, and state what you are ready to discuss.

runs.text: Stressed
describes strain or pressure.
Anxious
describes worry or unease.
Low
describes a down mood;
calm
describes a settled feeling.
Depressed
can describe a feeling in everyday speech or refer to a clinical condition. Feeling low or using the word does not by itself establish a diagnosis.
You can say “I'm struggling,” “I'm having a hard time coping,” or “This is affecting my sleep.”
Cope
means manage a difficult situation. “I've been up and down” means your experience or mood has varied. These are starting points; you decide how much detail to share.

turns.speaker: Person

runs.text: Do you have a few minutes? I'm having a hard time and could use someone to talk to.

turns.en: Do you have a few minutes? I'm having a hard time and could use someone to talk to.

turns.speaker: Friend

runs.text: I can talk for a bit. What would help right now?

turns.en: I can talk for a bit. What would help right now?

turns.speaker: Person

runs.text: I'd like you to listen. I'm not looking for advice yet.

turns.en: I'd like you to listen. I'm not looking for advice yet.

turns.speaker: Friend

runs.text: Okay. Tell me what you're comfortable sharing.

turns.en: Okay. Tell me what you're comfortable sharing.

runs.text: I've been overwhelmed lately.

blocks.caption: Ask a person for support · Person & Friend

runs.text: Overwhelmed

means feeling that demands or emotions are too much. A friend may also say “I care about you, but I can't give this enough attention right now. Could we talk later?” Availability and care are related but not identical. Requesting help does not require forced cheerfulness or immediate disclosure.

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: I'd like to ask about counseling appointments.

turns.en: I'd like to ask about counseling appointments.

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Would you prefer an in-person or video appointment?

turns.en: Would you prefer an in-person or video appointment?

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: In person, if possible. How do I arrange a first visit?

turns.en: In person, if possible. How do I arrange a first visit?

runs.text: I'll explain our intake process.

turns.speaker: Caller

runs.text: What does intake involve? What are the costs and privacy arrangements?

turns.en: What does intake involve? What are the costs and privacy arrangements?

blocks.caption: Ask about a service · Caller & Employee

runs.text: Intake
is the initial information-gathering process for a service.
Counselor / therapist
names a professional role; ask about the particular provider or kind of care. Do not assume a walk-in service, insurance coverage, or a confidentiality rule from the word
therapy
alone.

study.title: Describe and set boundaries in a session

turns.speaker: Therapist

runs.text: How is this affecting your day?

turns.en: How is this affecting your day?

turns.speaker: Client

runs.text: I'm having trouble concentrating, especially at work.

turns.en: I'm having trouble concentrating, especially at work.

turns.speaker: Therapist

runs.text: Could you tell me more about that?

turns.en: Could you tell me more about that?

turns.speaker: Client

runs.text: I can talk about work, but I'm not ready to discuss my family today.

turns.en: I can talk about work, but I'm not ready to discuss my family today.

turns.speaker: Therapist

runs.text: Let's stay with what you're ready to discuss.

turns.en: Let's stay with what you're ready to discuss.

blocks.caption: Describe and set boundaries in a session · Therapist & Client

runs.text: “So what you're saying is…” can introduce a summary. You can respond “Yes, that's close,” or “Not quite. I meant…” A
trigger
can name something that brings a strong reaction; explain what you mean rather than expecting the word to describe everyone's experience.

turns.speaker: Facilitator

runs.text: Would anyone like to share how the week has been?

turns.en: Would anyone like to share how the week has been?

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: I've had some difficult days, but today feels easier.

turns.en: I've had some difficult days, but today feels easier.

turns.speaker: Facilitator

runs.text: Thank you. Would you like to say more?

turns.en: Thank you. Would you like to say more?

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: I'll leave it there for now.

turns.en: I'll leave it there for now.

runs.text: “Can I pass for now?” requests not speaking at that point. Group arrangements differ, so ask about expectations rather than treating every group as identical. “These sessions have been helpful for me” reports one person's experience, not a promise that a method helps everyone.

Choose a fictional role rather than using private details if you prefer: trouble concentrating at work; wants listening rather than advice; interested in an in-person appointment; not ready to discuss family.
Ask a friend for time and state what kind of support you want. Partner asks “What would help?” Answer directly.
Ask a service about a first appointment, cost, and privacy. Partner offers an intake explanation. Ask what the word means.
Partner summarizes your concern incorrectly as “You're worried about your family.” Clarify your work concern and state your boundary.
In a group, share one short update or request to pass.
Solo: read the prompts and speak your turns; then hide the wording and try a different support need.
Possibilities:

“I'd like you to listen for now.” “Not quite—I'm talking about concentrating at work.” “I'd rather pass this time.” Check that the need, experience, and boundary are clear. These are communication exercises, not therapy or a diagnosis.
U.S. immediate-help reference:
For suicidal crisis or emotional distress, call or text
, the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For a life-threatening situation, use
. Do not call either number for this practice exercise.
NIMH help information

note: 今どんな支えがほしいかを伝えます。相談の場でも、今日は話したくないことや、まだ話す準備ができていないことを言えます。
